classification.difficultyReason: Infer rod-length ratios from the partitioned diagram, convert mixed expressions to a common unit, and test grouped and reciprocal relationships against the supplied claims.

inlines.text: Consider these rods, laid end to end. The pronumeral represents the length of a rod.
Use the diagram to answer these questions. Circle

spec.sourceRegion: Shared rod array and key above subquestion 1
spec.description: Four equal-total rows contain 3 p rods, 4 g rods, 6 r rods and 12 w rods. The horizontal key remains to the right, with proportional rod lengths and curved length annotations. Key rods are approximately two-thirds the scale of array rods, preserving the source-relative scale.
spec.mathematics: 3p = 4g = 6r = 12w; hence p = 4w, g = 3w and r = 2w. Purple, green and red fills identify corresponding rod types in the array and key; the w rods remain unfilled. Retained fill decision is tied to source SHA-256 c39163d967e8d231f0b642509eaa8c6760d834d94a87914407e2d8f05d993bdf.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, boundaries, key labels and colour relationships are permanent student-visible givens. No response answers appear in the diagram.

answer.worked:
From the diagram, $r=2w$ and $g=3w$.
$$\begin{align*}3r &= 3(2w) \\ 3r &= 6w \\ 3r &= 2g\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: $2g$.

From the diagram, $r=2w$ and $p=4w$.
$$\begin{align*}2w+r &= 2w+2w \\ 2w+r &= 4w \\ 2w+r &= p\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: $p$.

From the diagram, $g=3w$, $r=2w$ and $p=4w$.
$$\begin{align*}2g+3r &= 2(3w)+3(2w) \\ 2g+3r &= 12w \\ 2g+3r &= 3p\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: $3p$.

From the diagram, $g=3w$ and $r=2w$.
$$\begin{align*}6g &= 6(3w) \\ 6g &= 18w \\ 6g &= 9r\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: $9r$.

From the diagram, $r=2w$ and $p=4w$.
$$\begin{align*}8r &= 8(2w) \\ 8r &= 16w \\ 8r &= 4p\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: $4p$.

One $g$ rod equals three $w$ rods, so $w=\dfrac{g}{3}$. One $p$ rod equals four $w$ rods, so $w=\dfrac{p}{4}$.
Correct answer: Only Jo.

From the diagram, $r=2w$, $p=4w$ and $g=3w$, so $4g=12w$.
Jo:
$$\begin{align*}3(2w+r) &= 3(2w+2w) \\ 3(2w+r) &= 12w \\ 3(2w+r) &= 4g\end{align*}$$
Paul:
$$\begin{align*}2(p+2w) &= 2(4w+2w) \\ 2(p+2w) &= 12w \\ 2(p+2w) &= 4g\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: Both.
